Heaven plate · four lessons · three transmissions

Da Liu Ren: Lay Out the Chart

Da Liu Ren is one of the three classical methods (三式). It turns the twelve branches by the month general and the hour, then draws four lessons and three transmissions from the day. This page lays out the chart for a moment exactly as the Ming handbook 六壬大全 does, and shows the rule behind each step.

The moment

When is the question asked?

· The day turns at 23:00, the start of the 子 hour. The month general changes when the Sun reaches each mid-month solar term. The moment is set to now when the page opens.

Day or night noble

The book prefers the real sunrise and sunset, season by season, to a fixed hour: 「尤宜逐季推寻日出日入之时」

Enter the day, general and hour myself

For a chart from a book or a teacher: pick the day's 干支, the month general and the hour.

The chart is worked out on this device. Nothing is sent to us.

How the chart is built, in the book's words

The month general changes at each mid-month term, starting with 亥 after 雨水:

「雨水后日躔娵訾，正月将」

Each day stem lodges in a branch:

「甲课寅兮乙课辰，丙戊课巳不须论。丁己课未庚申上，辛戌壬亥是其真。癸课原来丑宫坐，分明不用四正神。」

The first transmission comes from a lesson where one side strikes the other; the middle and last follow up the heaven plate:

「取课先从下贼呼，如无下贼上克初。初传之上名中次，中上加临是末居。」

The noble star (貴人) by the day stem, day noble first:

「甲戊庚牛羊丑未，乙己鼠猴乡子申，丙丁猪鸡位亥酉，壬癸蛇兔藏巳卯」

辛 days: 午 by day, 寅 by night (the online copy prints 六壬 here, a slip for 六辛).

The other generals follow the noble, forward when it stands on 亥 to 辰, backward on 巳 to 戌:

「前有五位：一蛇、二雀、三合、四勾、五龙」

Quoted from 六壬大全 as printed (Chinese Wikisource), public domain.

Your chart (課式), as facts

—

Day 日
Month general 月將
Hour 時
Noble 貴人
Empty 旬空

Four lessons (四課)

Written right to left as in the book: lesson 1 is the heaven branch over the day stem's house, lesson 2 the branch over that; lessons 3 and 4 do the same from the day branch.

Three transmissions (三傳)

    How the first transmission was chosen

      Heaven plate on the earth plate (天地盤)

      Each square is a fixed earth branch (small). The large branch is the heaven branch standing on it, with the general riding it.

      Reading the chart

      The earth plate never moves; the heaven plate turns so that the month general sits on the hour. Every fact below is read off where heaven meets earth.

      The twelve generals (天將) ride the heaven plate, led by the noble. Their English names here are plain glosses of the Chinese.

      旬空 are the two branches the day's ten-day week leaves out; a transmission on one of them is marked empty. 「甲戌旬中用酉申」

      These are the facts the book reads from. Fate Tutor does not turn them into a forecast.

      What this page leaves out, and why

      The asker's birth year and running year (本命, 行年), the hidden stems (遁干), the many spirit stars (神煞) and the book's readings of each chart type are not shown. They turn the facts into judgements, and some touch topics Fate Tutor does not cover.

      The noble star follows the book's verse. The 1781 editors of the 四庫全書 noted that it keeps a common order, not the one they preferred: 「是书所取天乙尚沿俗例」

      Where the book disagrees with itself, the page follows the stated rule: one worked example in 卷九 starts 庚辰日 午時辰將 from 午, but the depth rule of 卷七 gives 寅.

      Where this comes from

      六壬大全

      All rules come from 六壬大全, a Ming handbook in twelve volumes with no author named, kept in the 1781 四庫全書 and public domain on Chinese Wikisource. 卷一 gives the rules for building the chart, 卷二 the month generals and the twelve generals, 卷四 the noble verse, and 卷七 the worked charts for each way of choosing the first transmission.

      Checked against the book: the engine gives the book's own worked charts, and over all 720 charts it gives the counts the book states (16 昴星, the nine 別責 days it names, one 獨足, six 井欄 days). The online copy has a few slips, such as 大雪 for 小雪 at the 寅 general; our checker names each one.

      About this tradition

      One of the three classical methods

      Da Liu Ren, with 奇門遁甲 and 太乙, makes up the three classical methods (三式). It is a chart of the moment a question is asked, built only from the day, the hour and the Sun's place among the solar terms.

      Fate Tutor lays out the chart and shows its sources. It does not turn a chart into a forecast, financial advice, medical advice or a decision made for you.

      These are traditional systems of belief. They are not science and they do not predict the future. Fate Tutor shows what each tradition says and where it says it, in the language of tendencies.
